query: The (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 high-entropy alloy is a solid refrigeration working medium that exhibits a large caloric response under applied-field and pressure-field operation but has poor load-bearing integrity and tends to crack. What single intervention could increase its integrity while preserving caloric performance in these operating regimes? State one hypothesis specifying the intervention, its proposed mechanism, predicted integrity and caloric outcomes relative to the unchanged alloy, applicable field, pressure, temperature, and loading boundaries, supporting prior evidence, and a controlled experiment with explicit results that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Introducing a minor amount (≈1 at%) of Nb into the (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 high-entropy alloy will refine the grain structure and promote beneficial precipitate formation at grain boundaries to enhance mechanical integrity without degrading the alloy’s caloric response under magnetic and pressure fields.
generation.material_initial_state: The undoped (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 alloy exhibits a substantial magnetic and barocaloric effect but has poor load-bearing integrity and shows a tendency to crack under mechanical loading.
generation.intervention: Add approximately 1 at% Nb during alloy synthesis (e.g., via arc melting followed by homogenization).
generation.conditions: Testing and operation under the same applied magnetic field and pressure-field regimes as the original alloy, and over temperature cycles that include the original caloric transition temperature.
generation.structural_mediator: Nb-induced grain refinement and the formation of Nb-rich precipitates at the grain boundaries, which act to blunt cracks and increase fracture toughness.
generation.mechanism: Nb doping encourages a finer grain structure and stabilizes grain boundary phases; these changes reduce local stress concentration sites and delay the onset of crack propagation, while the primary phase responsible for the caloric effect is preserved.
generation.predicted_outcome: The Nb-doped alloy is expected to show improved mechanical integrity (higher fracture toughness, delayed crack initiation) while maintaining similar levels of magnetic and barocaloric performance compared to the undoped alloy.
generation.baseline: The performance of the original (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 alloy in terms of crack resistance and caloric effect under identical field and temperature conditions.
generation.boundary: Applicable under refrigeration operating conditions with magnetic fields and pressures within the design limits; the hypothesis may not hold if the Nb content is significantly altered from ~1 at% or if the alloy is subjected to loading beyond its calibrated operational regime.
generation.uncertainty: The optimal Nb concentration and its exact influence on the multiphase microstructure and caloric properties remain uncertain without direct experimental validation.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two sets of samples: one set of the standard (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 alloy and one set doped with ≈1 at% Nb. Subject both sets to identical mechanical (tensile/compression) testing and evaluate their caloric responses under applied magnetic fields and pressure cycles.
measurements: Grain size and precipitate analysis using SEM/TEM
Fracture toughness and crack initiation/stress tests
Caloric response measurements (e.g., isothermal entropy change and adiabatic temperature change) using magnetometry and calorimetry
Differential scanning calorimetry (DSC) to confirm the phase transition temperature remains largely unchanged
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the Nb-doped samples do not show a statistically significant improvement in mechanical integrity (e.g., fracture toughness, delayed crack initiation) compared to the undoped samples, or if the caloric response (e.g., magnitude of entropy change) is degraded by more than an acceptable margin (e.g., >10%), then the hypothesis would be falsified.
